R&N_ITB,100,Scope Of Work,Civil Works,Earthworks,,,Civil Works Earthworks,"Backfill Compaction, Embankments, Non-Supportive Areas, Unpaved Areas, Supports, Roads, Paved Areas, Cap Layer 150 mm, Wind Erosion Protection, Soil-Cement Asphalt Paving, Polymer-Based Erosion Inhibitors, Gravel Layer 100 mm, Design Groundwater Level, Seasonal Groundwater Variation, Capillary Rise, Foundations On Backfilled Soil Prohibited, Settlement Requirement, Geotextile Layer, Geotechnical Recommendation, ASTM D 4253, ASTM D 4254, ASTM D 1557",Civil Works Earthworks Backfill Compaction Relative Density ASTM D 4253 ASTM D 4254 ASTM D 1557 Cap Layer 150 mm Wind Erosion Protection Groundwater Level Capillary Rise Geotextile,llm,Civil Works Earthworks Backfill Compaction Relative Density ASTM D 4253 ASTM D 4254 ASTM D 1557 Cap Layer 150 mm Wind Erosion Protection Groundwater Level Capillary Rise Geotextile,"Backfill placed for embankments, non-supportive and unpaved areas shall be compacted to at least 75% relative density (ASTM D 4253 and ASTM D 4254) for free draining soils containing less than 15% by weight finer than 75 micron sieve non plastic material or 90% of the maximum density as determined by ASTM D 1557for soils containing more than 15% material passing the 75 micron sieve.

A cap layer shall be placed to provide wind erosion protection in all the outdoor exposed areas. The cap layer shall be a minimum of 150 mm thick. The contractor to use soil-cement asphalt paving or sprayed-on polymer-based erosion inhibitors on that capping layer. Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered. R&N_ITB,101,Scope Of Work,Civil Works,Erosion Protection Works,,,Civil Works Erosion Protection Works,"Soil Stabilization With Cement, Soil-Cement Mixture, Optimum Moisture Content, Maximum Dry Density, 98% Maximum Dry Density, Type V Portland Cement, Erosion Control Blankets, Fibre Rolls, Coir Logs, Geo-Grids, Gravel Layer 100 mm",Civil Works Erosion Protection Works Soil Stabilization Cement Soil-Cement Mixture ASTM D-558 Type V Portland Cement ASTM C 150 Erosion Control Blankets Fibre Rolls Geo-Grids Gravel Layer 100 mm,llm,Civil Works Erosion Protection Works Soil Stabilization Cement Soil-Cement Mixture ASTM D-558 Type V Portland Cement ASTM C 150 Erosion Control Blankets Fibre Rolls Geo-Grids Gravel Layer 100 mm,"If the surface soils is susceptible to wind and water erosion these shall be stabilized with Cement. The soil and cement should be well mixed, moisture conditioned to within 1 per cent of optimum moisture and compacted to at least 98% of the maximum dry density. The optimum moisture content and maximum dry density of the soil-cement mixture should be determined by the ASTM D-558 test method. Traffic, except as required to maintain the surface of the soil cement in a damp condition, should not be permitted for at least 24 hours after final compaction.

For slope protection against erosion from wind, stabilization of surface soil with Type V Portland Cement as per ASTM C 150 may be adopted. For slope protection against erosion from water, slowing down of surface water is needed. To accomplish this, erosion control blankets, fibre rolls may be used. Erosion control blankets are usually woven type from a chosen material, with lots of ridges and obstructions. These materials are either synthetic or natural. Fibber rolls are also made of similar material as used in erosion control blankets but are rolled into large diameter logs. Coir type logs/ Logs made of rice/wheat straw also may be used. These logs are nailed into the slope to slow down the surface water. Tensar type geo-grids also may be effective. The source/ availability of the appropriate material is essential in selection of the technique, and it shall be duly approved by the Owner's engineer.

Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. R&N_ITB,109,Scope Of Work,Civil Works,Surfacing,,,Civil Works Surfacing,"Concrete Paving 150 mm, Asphalt Paving, 1.2 m, 5.0 m, Slope To Drainage, Surface Water Drainage System, Storm Water Drainage System, Roof Drainage, 100 Years Rainfall Return Period, Basements Drainage, Cable Trenches Drainage, Pipe Trenches Drainage, Tunnels Drainage, Sumps, Sump Pump, Storm Water Catch Pits, Sub-Soil Drainage, Hazardous Areas, ESIA, Storm Water Basin, API, NFPA",Civil Works Surfacing Surface Water Drainage System Storm Water Drainage System 150 mm concrete paving asphalt paving 100 years rainfall return period roof drainage sumps sump pump storm water basin ESIA API NFPA,llm,Civil Works Surfacing Surface Water Drainage System Storm Water Drainage System 150 mm concrete paving asphalt paving 100 years rainfall return period roof drainage sumps sump pump storm water basin ESIA API NFPA,"All buildings in the Plant shall be paved with minimum 150 mm concrete extending from the edge of the building  for  a  distance  of  1.2m  with  proper  slope  to  drainage  Surface  Water  Drainage  System  and additionally asphalted paving shall be extending from 1.2 m up to a distance of 5.0m with proper slope to drainage Surface Water Drainage System if the soil is erosion prone due to water and wind.

A surface water drainage system shall be provided for the Plant. The design shall allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of surface water over the whole of the Site (arising from run-off of natural water from buildings, roads, ground surface, paved areas, etc.). All buildings shall be provided with roof drainage for disposal of surface water, and be connected to the surface water drainage system. The surface water drainage system shall be arranged and designed to effectively manage all run-off and discharge arising from the Site.
The Storm  water  Drainage  system  shall  be  designed  considering  100  years  rainfall  return  period  and rainfall intensity equal to the retention period.

Basements, cable and pipe trenches and tunnels shall be constructed with adequate provision for drainage. Floors to basements, trenches and tunnels shall be laid to falls and/or drainage channels provided therein. Any water entering the basements trenches or tunnels shall be routed to sumps and connected to the surface water drainage system. Where connection to the surface water drainage system is not practical, then provision to pump-out water from the trench or tunnel drainage sump, by permanent and/or portable sump pumps shall be made. Fire deluge water shall be gathered into storm water catch pits and discharged via main storm water system and prevented from entering tunnels.
Primary site drainage and sub-soil drainage shall be provided, where necessary, on external areas generally to protect the site from run off into building areas etc.

Storm water drainage sumps, pumps and electrical equipment shall be located to avoid hazardous areas. If unavoidable then the pumps and electrical equipment shall conform to the requirements in accordance with API and NFPA for operation in hazardous environments. column1: R&N_ITB,116,Scope Of Work,Civil Works,Concrete Requirements,,,Civil Works Concrete Requirements,"Concrete Embedment, Embedded Items, Stainless Steel, Carbon Steel, Sub-Plate, Welding Plant Fixings, Corrosion Protection Coatings, Anchor Bolts, Concrete Cover 100 mm, Concrete Construction Tolerances, ACI 117, Spread Footings, Lateral Separation B/2, Bearing Capacity, Settlement Estimates, Tanks, Differential Settlement 15%, Landscaping 3 m Clearance, Concrete Or Asphalt Apron 1.2 m, Surface Water Drainage, Impermeable Membrane 1.5 m, Water Lines Away From Foundations",Civil Works Concrete Requirements Concrete Embedment Corrosion Protection Anchor Bolts 100 mm ACI 117 Spread Footings Separation B/2 Tanks Settlement Landscaping Apron Drainage Impermeable Membrane,llm,Civil Works Concrete Requirements Concrete Embedment Corrosion Protection Anchor Bolts 100 mm ACI 117 Spread Footings Separation B/2 Tanks Settlement Landscaping Apron Drainage Impermeable Membrane,"The materials that will be used for embedded items shall of stainless steel or carbon steel (e.g. sub-plate) as per proven experience and aggressiveness of the environment. The selection of material will be based on strength and durability requirements. Additionally, the choice of material may be dictated by interfacing issues with plant requirements.

The  necessity  of  welding  plant  fixings  etc.  to  embedment  exposed  at  the  concrete  surface  in  exposed environments shall be considered at design stage and wherever possible alternative fixing details shall be provided in order to preserve the original corrosion protective coatings.

Where this detail cannot be designed out then to protect the embedded item(s) from corrosion, for the life of the station, the following minimum material requirements and corrosion protection criteria shall be provided.
- All anchor bolts shall have a concrete cover of at least 100 mm.

The  corrosion  protection  system  provided  to  concrete  embedment  shall  also  consider  the  corrosion protection system(s) provided to adjacent plant and the dual requirements shall be considered collectively, where applicable, to select the most appropriate solution.
Concrete construction tolerances shall comply with ACI 117.

The minimum lateral distance between adjacent individual spread footings bearing at the same grade on soil shall be B/2, where B is the footing width or diameter of the larger footing. For Square or rectangular footings, of width B, the minimum lateral separation distance should be no less than B.  Where the lateral spacing  is  less  than  recommended,  the  stress  distribution  between  the  adjacent  footings  should  be analysed.

Net design bearing capacities and settlement estimates for tanks shall be based on the assumption that the foundation soils underlying the tank are not significantly affected by adjacent tanks. The lateral distance between adjacent tanks should be limited to a distance B, where B is the diameter of the smaller of two adjacent tanks. If the tanks are spaced at a distance less than B, the differential settlement between the centre and edge could be about 15 percent larger.

Furthermore, the landscaping shall be at least 3 m away from the proposed structure perimeters. A 1.2-m wide concrete or asphalt apron could be constructed adjacent to buildings around the perimeters to protect the foundation soils from surface water and sloped away from the structures to facilitate drainage. Water lines should, if possible, be kept away from the foundations.  In addition, consideration should be given to the use of an impermeable membrane placed around building perimeters to a distance of approximately 1.5 m beyond the edge of the foundations and sloped away from structures to provide drainage.",[Ukudu] TREATED WATER TANK FOUNDATION (CCPP PLANT AREA)_REBAR DETAIL (최종점수: 0.9335 / 기본: 0.7835),[Muara Tawar] [Clean and Dirty Oil Tank Foundation(For Block 2)]_Re-bar Arrangement (최종점수: 0.9329 / 기본: 0.7829),"[Grati] Raw Water Tank Concrete Structure Foundation Plan, Detail & Schedule (최종점수: 0.9321 / 기본: 0.7821)","[Muara Tawar] [Clean and Dirty Oil Tank Foundation(For Block 3, 4)]_Re-bar Arrangement (최종점수: 0.9321 / 기본: 0.7821)",[Fadhili] POTABLE WATER TANK FOUNDATION REBAR DETAIL (최종점수: 0.9301 / 기본: 0.7801),[Fadhili] DEMINERALIZED WATER TANK FOUNDATION REBAR DETAIL (최종점수: 0.9269 / 기본: 0.7769),[Fadhili] POTABLE & FIRE FIGHTING WATER TANK FOUNDATION REBAR DETAIL (최종점수: 0.9256 / 기본: 0.7756),[Ukudu] ULSD STORAGE TANK FOUNDATION (CCPP PLANT AREA)_REBAR DETAIL (최종점수: 0.9230 / 기본: 0.7730),[Fadhili] EMBEDDED CONDUIT LAYOUT FOR POTABLE STORAGE WATER TANK & FIRE WATER TANK AREA (최종점수: 0.9215 / 기본: 0.7715),[Ukudu] UF FEED WATER TANK FOUNDATION (CCPP PLANT AREA)_REBAR DETAIL (최종점수: 0.9209 / 기본: 0.7709),"[Grati] Make up Demin Water Tank Concrete Structure Foundation Plant, Detail & Schedule (최종점수: 0.9208 / 기본: 0.7708)",[Grati] Calculation Sheet for Raw Water Tank Foundation (최종점수: 0.9193 / 기본: 0.7693),[Fadhili] EMBEDDED CONDUIT LAYOUT FOR DEMI WATER STORAGE TANK AREA (최종점수: 0.9186 / 기본: 0.7686),[Ukudu] ULSD BUFFER TANK FOUNDATION AND ULSD SLUDGE PIT (CCPP PLANT AREA)_REBAR DETAIL (최종점수: 0.9177 / 기본: 0.7677),[Fadhili] CALCULATION OF POTABLE WATER TANK FOUNDATION (최종점수: 0.9168 / 기본: 0.7668),"[Ukudu] ULSD PUMP AND TREATMENT SHELTER_BEAM, SLAB & MISC. Fire protection to the structural steelworks/ steel structures which are exposed to lube oil fire, shall be intumescent paint system in exposed solutions, and fire-resistant board system or vermiculite or spray system in concealed areas to give 2 hour fire protection when tested in accordance with NFPA.

- SMACNA Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors National Association.
- NFPA National Fire Protection Association.
- ARI American Refrigeration Institute.
- ANSI American National Standards Institute.
- AABC Associated Air Balance Council.

All systems shall be designed and installed to provide acceptable environmental conditions for each area. The conditions of temperature, humidity, air movement and air filtration shall be controlled as required in the respective areas in summer and winter.
HVAC  systems  serving  critical  areas  such  as  Control  Rooms  shall  be  provided  with  duty/standby  air handling and mechanical cooling plant to ensure continuity of operation.

HVAC systems shall be arranged to shut down in the event of a fire alarm, with installation of the fire dampers for each individual room, seal supply and extract ducts as required for the application of clean agent fire suppression systems and start up smoke control pressurization systems. Provision shall be made in all plant areas for the venting and clearance of smoke and fumes in the event of fire, by means of roof vents or extract fans.

All systems and components shall be suitable for the design life of the Plant, and be designed for minimum life cycle cost and complexity, consistent with functionality, ease of maintenance and reliability.

For all general cases the HVAC  systems  the ambient design conditions shall be  as  ASHRAE recommendations to suite the site conditions. The HVAC systems shall be designed to obtain the internal conditions  and  system  redundancy  as  indicated  in  the  OTS.  Central  air-conditioning  systems  having humidity control may be provided with air handling units for fresh air supply. These units shall be provided with cooling coils and steam humidifiers to handle the full dehumidification/humidification load for the central  system,  with  dew  point  control.  Fresh  air-cooling  coils  shall  have  10 per  cent  margin  on  heat transfer  surface  to  cater  for  periods  of  abnormally  high  humidity.  Face  air  velocity  shall  not  exceed 2.0 m/sec.
Humidification shall be by electric powered steam generators with proportional control and steam lance injection.
